children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

This will help me determine which eligibility path we need to follow. The eligibility rules differ based on whether a child is:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old (where education/training status matters)
- 20 or over

Please share this information so we can continue with your assessment.

conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 19 and lives with me at home. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below, or similar qualifications)?
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

**1. Is Alex's A-level study full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - not counting homework or self-study)

**2. Is this education funded by an employer or linked to a job agreement with an employer?** (For example, some apprenticeships or employer-sponsored programs wouldn't qualify)

Please let me know these details about Alex's A-level studies.

conversation.author: actor

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **Not Eligible**

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** based on his current circumstances.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

While Alex meets several of the eligibility criteria:
- ✓ He's 19 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- ✓ He's in approved non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- ✓ His education is full-time (12+ hours per week of supervised study)

**However**, the key issue is:
- ✗ He's working 24 or more hours per week in paid employment

Under Child Benefit rules, a young person aged 16 or over who works 24+ hours per week does not qualify as a "qualifying child," even when they are simultaneously attending approved full-time education.

### What this means:

Child Benefit is designed to support families with children who are either not working or working limited hours. Once a 16-19 year old works 24+ hours per week, they're considered to have moved into substantial employment, regardless of their education status.

### If circumstances change:

If Alex's work hours reduce to less than 24 hours per week while he continues his A-level studies, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him again. You would need to make a new claim or notify HMRC of the change in circumstances.

I know this isn't the outcome you were hoping for, especially given how hard Alex is working to balance both his studies and employment. If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to reach out.
